purpose: Publication-quality figures — hydrographs, FDCs, scatter plots, maps

plt.savefig.note: Always call plt.close(fig) after saving to release memory. Use dpi=300 for publication.

ax.set_yscale.note: For FDCs and hydrographs, log scale exposes low-flow behaviour. Use 'log' not 'symlog'.

gotchas: plt vs fig/ax: plt.plot() operates on the current axes — safe for quick scripts. In functions, always use fig, ax = plt.subplots() to avoid state leakage between tests.
Memory leak: not calling plt.close(fig) after saving leaves the figure open. In loops, use plt.close('all') at the end.
log scale with zeros: ax.set_yscale('log') will fail silently or raise if the data contains 0 or negative values. Clip: q = np.clip(q, 1e-6, None).
Twin axes alignment: ax2 = ax.twinx() shares the x-axis. Tick labels on ax2 don't align with ax1 by default — use ax2.set_yticks(...).
Colour-blind palettes: default matplotlib tab10 is not colour-blind friendly. Use seaborn's 'colorblind' palette or matplotlib's 'tab10' with explicit colours.
Tight layout: fig.tight_layout() can fail with colorbars. Use constrained_layout=True in plt.subplots(constrained_layout=True) instead.
Date axis: matplotlib stores dates as floats internally. Use mdates.DateFormatter and mdates.AutoDateLocator for clean tick labels on time axes.
DPI and figure size: default figsize=(6.4, 4.8) at dpi=100. For publication (column width ~3.5 inches): figsize=(3.5, 2.5), dpi=300.

common_patterns.hydrograph:
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
ax.plot(dates, obs, label='Observed', color='steelblue')
ax.plot(dates, sim, label='Simulated', color='tomato', linestyle='--')
ax.set_ylabel('Discharge (m³/s)')
ax.legend()
fig.savefig('hydrograph.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close(fig)
common_patterns.fdc:
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
exceedance = np.linspace(0, 100, len(q_sorted))
ax.semilogy(exceedance, q_sorted)
ax.set_xlabel('Exceedance probability (%)')
ax.set_ylabel('Discharge (m³/s)')
common_patterns.dual_axis:
fig, ax1 = plt.subplots()
ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax1.bar(dates, precip, color='steelblue', alpha=0.4, label='P')
ax2.plot(dates, q, color='tomato', label='Q')
